The sad reality is that politics, especially campaign politics, has always been a heavily partisan and biased public sport where just about everybody picks a side. And more and more over the last few years people, parties, and various organizations spend more time slinging mud at those who have made different choices than anything else. Possibly in some parallel dimension Canadian politics is covered and discussed in an unbiased and factual way but in the here and now everyone has an opinion, including journalists and editors, and the freedom (subject to, as the SCoC tells us, reasonable restrictions) to express that opinion.

YMMV of course but rewriting headlines to create unbiased, sanitized, and/or non-partisan post titles presents a potentially slippery slope - does the sanitizing end at the headline? Does it include potentially inflammatory and/or politically biased statements in opinion columns? Does it include the out of context sound bites the parties themselves choose to deceptively use to swap public opinion?

And then we have the ultimate question of who is the final arbitrator of what is or is not considered overly partisan, or what is or is not considered overly biased, or what is or is not considered overly inflammatory? And the inevitable follow up question that will be asked by those who run afoul of the rule - does that final arbitrator have an agenda of their own?

If the headlines are left "as printed" the subverse can accuse the media outlet of bias and call them out on that, if we have posts or users disappearing as a result of this rule being enforced by one or more moderators they will be the ones to bear the brunt of the subverses displeasure and complaints should there be even an inkling of bias. And there is in this the potential for much drama.

Again, I am not trying to be argumentative here. I just see greater potential issues and controversy being created than the rule change is intended to address.
